angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 473,076 km at 59.48 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 16.8113 +/- 0.0307 mas (same row, RUWE 1.33): 59.48 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.68 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2411 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract): 473,076 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.65 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2411 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4099 +/- 123 K from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2411 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2411 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2411.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.586, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
